children: Patanjali Foods shares rose up to 4 per cent in Tuesday's trading session after the company's management backed its growth targets for FY27.

The stock hit an intraday high of Rs 412.80 per share on the NSE, gaining more than 4 per cent. Profit booking emerged at higher levels, and the stock was quoting at Rs 400.35 per share, up 1.05 per cent, around 12:45 pm.

The stock had gained 8 per cent in the previous session after the company's management struck an optimistic note on its FY27 growth prospects, particularly in FMCG and edible oils, while also forecasting strong free cash flow.

Sanjeev Asthana, CEO of Patanjali Foods, told CNBC-TV18 that the company expects its FMCG business to grow 18-20 per cent in FY27, while the foods business is projected to expand 8-10 per cent. Edible oils are expected to register growth of more than 4 per cent.
Asthana said the company was confident of meeting its FY27 targets and expects to generate free cash flow of Rs 700-800 crore during the year.

The management's commentary on consumer demand was mixed. Asthana said urban demand remained strong and the festive season was expected to be good, but the company was less optimistic about rural demand due to the poor monsoon.
Supply conditions in edible oils are another concern. According to Asthana, more than 90 per cent of India's sunflower oil imports are currently stuck, making supply a major issue.

The latest management outlook follows a strong June-quarter performance. Patanjali Foods' consolidated net profit surged 86 per cent year-on-year to Rs 335.7 crore in Q1 FY27, while revenue from operations rose 29 per cent to Rs 11,337.5 crore.
EBITDA increased 69 per cent to Rs 543.3 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 4.8 per cent from 3.7 per cent a year earlier.
The June quarter marked the company's fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue.

title: Patanjali Foods shares rise up to 4%, extend gains for third straight day on FY27 growth targets
